newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH TAX DEBATE AT A GLANCE - POSSIBLE SCENARIOS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH TAX DEBATE AT A GLANCE - POSSIBLE SCENARIOS.

text.p: The Polish Senate on Thursday
continued its debate on tax bills which will determine the
shape of the 1997 budget. Its vote was expected late in the day
or on Friday.
The government, which has submitted a budget draft based on
1996 tax levels and assuming a deficit at 2.6 percent of gross
domestic product, last month offered a moderate tax cut which
would keep the deficit unchanged from this year's planned level
of 2.8 percent of GDP.
But the government proposals were rejected on October 24 by
the lower house of parliament, the Sejm.
The ruling coalition's Peasant party (PSL) voted with the
opposition to defeat its larger partner, the Democratic Left
Alliance (SLD), the only party to back the government scheme.
The Sejm instead passed a four-level tax scale sharply
cutting taxes for the lowest-paid, despite government protests
that this would increase the deficit and bring inflation.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski has signalled that he
supports the government scheme and will veto the tax bill if
the Senate passes the lower house's proposed tax levels.
Since then, Peasant senators and senate committees have
proposed alternative tax levels. The issue could end in several
ways, depending on how the Peasants and opposition behave.
Here is a summary of some tax proposals and their impact on
the 1997 budget, as estimated by the Finance Ministry.
TAX RATES (pct) 1997 BUDGET
change in revenues deficit
bln PLN pct GDP
Sejm bill 17, 20, 33, 45 -3.6 3.0 plus
Government 20, 31, 43 -2.0 2.8
PSL senators 18, 20, 33, 44 n.a. n.a.
Senate committees 20, 32, 44 n.a. n.a.
SOME POSSIBLE SCENARIOS
* The Senate passes the lower house's tax rates. The bill
goes to President Kwasniewski, who has 20 days to sign it into
law or veto it. If he applies the veto as he has suggested, the
bill goes back to the Sejm, which needs a two-thirds majority
to overrule the veto. The SLD has 167 out of 460 seats, more
than the one-third needed to uphold the veto. It does so.
OUTCOME - Tax rates remain unchanged, as parliament cannot
pass another bill before the November 30 deadline for tax
changes. Budget deficit of 2.6 percent of GDP in 1997.
According to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz the
government will propose a limited amendment to the current tax
law to eliminate some tax breaks and loopholes.
* The Senate amends the tax bill in line with a private
member's bill similar to government proposals. The lower house
votes next week, the Peasants or the opposition relent and the
bill passes, going to the President who immediately signs it so
that the bill takes effect before the November 30 deadline.
OUTCOME - Lower taxes, deficit at 2.8 percent of GDP.
* The Senate amends the tax bill to conform with the
government plan but the lower house finds a sufficient majority
(more than 50 percent of those voting) to reject the changes.
The original Sejm bill goes to the President, who vetoes it.
OUTCOME - Tax rates unchanged, deficit at 2.6 percent.
* The Senate amends the tax bill according to the Senate
committees' proposals, the Sejm passes it and Kwasniewski signs
it into law.
OUTCOME - Tax rates lowered but by less than in the
government plan. Budget deficit probably slightly below 2.8
percent.
* The Senate amends the tax bill in line with the
committees' proposals, PSL and opposition vote together in the
lower house and reject it, the Sejm bill remains intact, which
Kwasniewski vetoes.
OUTCOME - Tax rates unchanged, deficit at 2.6 percent.
* The Senate amends the tax bill according to the PSL
proposal, the SLD fails to garner a sufficient majority to
reject it, but Kwasniewski vetoes the bill.
OUTCOME - Tax rates unchanged, deficit at 2.6 percent.
* The Senate amends the tax bill acccording to the PSL
proposal, the lower house rejects it, the Sejm bill remains
intact, which Kwasniewski vetoes.
OUTCOME - Taxes rates unchanged, deficit at 2.6 percent.
* The ruling coalition strikes a last-minute compromise,
which envisages a deeper tax cut than the government proposal
but less radical than the Sejm's, the bill clears the Senate
and the lower house, President Kwasniewski signs it into law.
OUTCOME - Taxes lowered on a yet undetermined scale, budget
deficit probably in the 2.8-3.0 percent range.
